Also the way I read and keep track knowledge is also a bit chaotic, I hear about concepts but then don’t know where to find it back, need to work on this. Obviously it works because we manage to anticipate and build models that anticipates the future well, but still, in terms of business, it’s still needed, MBB, STB, TPB are all good stocks underlying so yeah, business still wins.

entry.title: Learning 09/08/2025
entry.content:
Catch up on the market
Market drops again with more than 2 billion dollar in volume. It’s been a while since I look at the market but since it’s in an elevated level, not much opportunity I could find I guess. Apparently my graham stocks still overperform the market thanks solely to HSL position (this is a hypothetical position btw)

Catch up on the news
Kraft and Heinz has been separated and Buffett is not happy, this is a complex deal so I’m not gonna dive in too deep about it.
TTA apparently has people buying in. The stock has really high EBITDA margin for some reason. Not much happening anyway. No M&A news that I’ve spotted yet this year

Learning
Read through these insights by Rob Vinall, can tell that he’s also another smart guy that I should follow: https://www.rvcapital.ch/post/first-half-2025-letter-to-co-investors. I’ve been quite detached recently but people like these make it fun to absorb and learn. He has some amazing insights about the AI era we’re living in and what could happen to navigate on the market. AI is similar to the dot-com bubble is that it’s a new game changing technology, and we’re seeing the same things where it’s not the company itself that is profitable, it’s provider, i.e NVIDIA, TSMC, and so on. I love his analogy, “companies selling shovels in a gold rush”. Absolutely correct, the AI players are not profitable (yet), only the shovels one. Similar to dotcom, the networking companies like Cisco makes money. Maybe even the best AI companies/businesses are not founded yet (he mentions that could you predict Uber, Facebook, and Google, so on when the dot com just get started). This is the time to not think about what you can do with AI, but what’s profitable with AI that create a huge moat around it, a trillion dollar idea. Of course I don’t care about it but just thinking about it would be helpful and fun. Obviously most people are just zoning on the capability of AI, even best think leaders right now zone in on the capabilities, not the business model.

entry.title: Learning 08/25/2025
entry.content:
Catch up on the market The market took another dive, should I have take a quick profit with my STB? probably not since the situation has not fully played out (meaning at least 100% on it). I don’t really care about it right now and I could forget about, only MBB is worth selling and I was right. Other positions are dropping and I love to add more for example FIT Catch up on the news Interesting news (https://vietstock.vn/2025/08/gilimex-lo-ky-luc-quy-2-co-phieu-van-tang-tran-nho-ky-vong-vu-kien-amazon-737-1345176.htm). Where one of the stocks is dealing with Amazon and Amazon suddenly drops its order. The business is terrible but the catalyst could add 2 trillion dong to the company, the risk is that it could go wrong and Gilimex lose 1/3 of its equity. Also interestingly there’s a probable Vietnamese lawyer graduated from Harvard and Stanford Law School.

Learning
There is analysis about what makes a good bank by John Huber (https://sabercapitalmgt.com/wells-fargo-
vs-small-community-banks/)
A good yardstick for earnings about bank is actually PTPP (Pre-tax, pre-provision earnings), as well as pre tax earnings. Like its name, earnings before tax and money set aside (provisions) for future credit loss. A good yard stick is to take an average rather than care about abnormally high provisions, which often create confusion among lesser knowledgable investor.
High ROE and Pretax return on tangible equity (ROTE), obviously, higher rate of return on capital means the bank can make more money with similar investment, in turn, higher stock price growth organically
A new thing I learn is the cost of deposits, meaning banks with lower interest rate often will have lower cost, in turn they can use that money into their high ROE and generate higher money, despite lower interest rate mean the bank is less attractive but money from deposits is not the key indicator of banks.
A final big thing is the economy of scale (an economy), meaning bigger the bank, the lower the cost and also wider network across the country.
So next time look at bank, look at the cost, the assets as well as the number of bank network, the ROE, ROTE, during the depressed market.

entry.title: Learning 08/19/2025
entry.content:
Catch up on the market
The market still goes up, I sold MBB since it’s a bit overpriced and all of the big funds are focused on selling. I also bought SGN at the bottom of Darvas box, this is a bit speculative but if it turns to bad, I will just continue hold it

Catch up on the news
Read a bit about OpenAI through Altman interview and it seems like OpenAI is still operating in a loss, heavy loss, despite revenue is insane. AI is obviously not a good business because the cost of training far exceeds the value of subscription as well as API calls. However, it looks like most of the cost is just upfront cost from servers, electricity, and sga, it should only profitable when the revenue pass a certain mark and maintain healthy margin from there. Still not sure if this is the greatest business on the planet. Like Buffett and Howard Marks, the most important breakthrough might not be the greatest business on the planet.

entry.content:
Catch up on the market
Market still rises while most of my positions have a slight downturn, well I ask my dad but there’s too many details so it’s not fit to tell me right now, but I should still sell pretty soon before things turn bad. I think MBB is at the top now so I will half my position

Catch up on the news
Apparently there’s bunch of insitutional buy and sell https://vietstock.vn/2025/08/lanh-dao-mua-ban-co-phieu-loat-thuong-vu-thoai-von-sap-dien-ra-739-1342776.htm
FTS is selling its shares in MSH (Song Hong Textile), looks through the number is interesting.
An article talks about EVF fundamental business is hard to understand, may be intersting to look at since the more misunderstood, the better the opportunity https://vietstock.vn/2025/08/8216khong-the-do-ket-qua-kinh-doanh-cua-evn-bang-loi-hay-lo8217-768-1342775.htm
New news on new positions of big value investor as well, Michael Burry started buying again, as well as Berkshire Hathaway, who bought UnitedHealth.

Learning
From the book about Bezos and Amazon and his thinking about narrative fallacy coined by Taleb in Black Swan (which I haven’t read). Basically, people can easily fall into the trap of simplifying any phenomenon, be it in the stock market or whatever into a simple causation, even though it’s inherently have no connection. For example, I remember some philosophy concept by Hume or something says Day Happen after Night, which means Day causes Night, which is just inherently wrong. The same with stock market, I fell into this where as a catalyst, banks set high target for credit = bank stocks rises, or divestment from SCIC = stock rises, which in fact they have no inherent connection. Looks like other executives must read Black Swan at Amazon as well.
